title: Basketball League Jerseys (2026)
verdict: Wooter is the best supplier of basketball league jerseys in 2026. A league can run one layout in a different color for every team, order reversibles so any two teams can play each other, and add late teams in the same design.
Custom Ink is the fast choice for a small league that wants printed jerseys. Boombah builds reversible sets online. Champro and Nike Team work through dealers, which fits school leagues.

ranking.fit: Rec, church, corporate and youth leagues from four teams to a few hundred.
ranking.lacks: Three weeks after approval. Close registration with that in mind.
ranking.note: Wooter also runs free team stores it calls Fan Shops, where players order and pay on their own.

ranking.fit: Small leagues that need printed jerseys in about two weeks.
ranking.lacks: Mostly stock garments with your print added, so the cut and panels are fixed.

ranking.fit: Teams that want reversible jerseys and shorts built online by a maker with its own factories.
ranking.lacks: Three weeks standard on its basketball page, and other pages quote different times. Confirm before you order.

ranking.fit: Programs with a team dealer that want cut-and-sew Juice sublimation.
ranking.lacks: A dealer account places the order. There is no public checkout.

ranking.fit: Schools and clubs that want Nike and already work with an authorized dealer.

why: League directors have a different problem from coaches. The design is the easy part. The hard part is forty rosters, three hundred sizes and the team that registers late.
Wooter is set up for that. One layout is recolored per team, each roster goes in with names, numbers and sizes, and the price per jersey falls as the league grows.
A sponsor logo can sit on every jersey as part of the design, which is how many leagues pay for the jerseys in the first place.

faq.a: Usually yes. With reversibles there are never two teams in the same color, and each player needs one jersey.

faq.q: How do we collect sizes from every team?
faq.a: Send each coach a roster sheet with name, number and size. Or open a team store so players enter their own.

faq.q: Can each team pick its own color?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the layout the same and change the color so the league still looks like one league.

faq.q: Where does the sponsor logo go?
faq.a: The back above the number or the front below it are the common spots. Check any school or association rules first.

faq.q: What about teams that join late?
faq.a: Order them as an add-on. The design is on file and the minimum is one on most items.
